findings.title: Cover and hearing close two reception routes
findings.claim: The focus presents rejection as a coordinated closure of reception: the eyes are covered away from the reminder while hearing cannot be reached.
findings.mechanism: The eye-cover-reminder relation blocks visual access, and the capacity verb with hearing names a second route of uptake; together the clauses turn one failure into paired visual and auditory closure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the focus as a condition of blocked uptake, not merely two unrelated sensory details.
findings.containment: The ordinary covered-eyes and inability-to-hear statement remains intact; this finding describes their local coordination and does not decide whether hearing is physical, attentive, or obedient.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel and exact focus occurrences support the coordinated relation, while the synthesis of the two predicates as paired reception closure remains a bounded macro inference.

findings.containment: This is a cross-root analogy, not an etymological equivalence: the ordinary focus cover remains a blockage from the reminder, while the garden and lodging remain their own context images.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 18:107 coordinates are exact and the HFT explicitly supplies the function contrast, but the cross-root synthesis is surprising exploratory attributed evidence.

branch_activations.carrier: The supplied garden occurrence carries the HFT-attributed covered enclosure that shelters cultivated life.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus cover and the lodging occurrence supply the contrasting blocked and receptive functions.
branch_activations.activation: The garden carrier contacts the focus cover through shared enclosure imagery while its relation to lodging supplies a different effect on reception.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: A covered enclosure can shelter reception when its function turns toward cultivation and welcome.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent lexicon gloss or facet is supplied for this context branch, and garden is not made synonymous with cover.

findings.title: The added worship-and-aid overlay
findings.claim: The added 1:5 overlay places the focus's failed hearing beside a direct act of worship and request for help, so the blocked route can also be perceived as a blocked entry into obedient dependence.
findings.mechanism: The focus hearing branch includes understanding, acceptance, and obedience; the external carriers in 1:5 name worship and seeking aid, giving that receptive faculty a concrete positive destination beyond the native pericope.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the focus's inability as a missing relation to the addressed One, not only a missing sensory event.
findings.containment: This is a Phase-2 external overlay and does not make 1:5 part of the native pericope or replace the focus's plain sensory wording; the cross-context relation remains bounded because the external member has no separate trust label.

epistemic.reason: The external worship and aid surfaces and the focus return are supplied exactly, while their positive-destination relation is a bounded Phase-2 inference without a separate support trust label.

branch_activations.boundary: The overlay does not claim that 1:5 explains the native focus historically or that every hearing use means worship.
